raw_response:
1. Frame 1 shows a dark, nearly black background with a large, very dark hexagonal silhouette centered in the frame, and a light grey polygonal surface in the upper-middle area. The light surface is much wider than it is tall, with a thin light outline and thin light interior lines that radiate from a single convergence point located close to its upper (far) edge; the lines run from that point toward the left corner, the right corner, and the lower corners of the outline. The fill has a soft radial shading gradient, brightest near the middle of the surface and darker toward the left and right corners. No text, numbers, scale bars, or axes are visible. At the very top of the frame there is a slightly darker horizontal band, but I do not see any bright colored overlay bar in this frame.
2. Frame 2 shows the same scene: the same dark background, the same large dark hexagonal silhouette in the same position, and a light grey surface with the same overall outline and screen position as frame 1. The difference is in the interior lines: they form a six-spoke pattern that converges at a point near the middle of the outline (close to its visual centroid), with spokes running toward the left corner, the right corner, and the remaining outline corners. The fill again has a soft radial gradient, brightest slightly right of the convergence point. No text or scale reference is visible; the same slightly darker band appears at the very top.
3. Differences: the interior line pattern. In frame 1 the spokes converge near the upper (far) edge of the outline, so the upper triangles read as thin slivers and the lower part of the surface reads as large sloping facets — a shallow tent-like appearance. In frame 2 the spokes converge near the center of the outline, so the six triangles read as roughly symmetric and the surface reads as a flat fan. In frame 2 the bottom outline shows a slight downward point at its center that is weaker or absent in frame 1 (low confidence). Identical (or apparently identical): the outer outline and screen position of the light surface, the dark hexagonal silhouette and its position, the background, the overall lighting and shading pattern, and the absence of any text or overlay.
4. Frame 1: the convergence point sits very close to the upper (far) edge of the outer boundary — clearly above the visual center of the surface; the far edge passes essentially through or just inside the convergence point (uncertainty: the offset from the edge is at most a few pixels as I read it, and the lines are faint, so I cannot say whether it touches the edge or sits just inside it). Frame 2: the convergence point sits near the middle of the outline, close to its centroid, slightly above the vertical midline and slightly right of the horizontal midline as I read it (uncertainty: moderate; the spokes are faint and my reading of "slightly" is by eye). I cannot convert either position into a height or distance.
5. There is no scale reference anywhere in either frame; the view is a single oblique perspective with strong vertical foreshortening (the surface is roughly five times wider than tall on screen), which compresses any vertical offset into a small screen-space shift; the interior lines are thin and low-contrast; the fill is shaded by lighting rather than by distinct per-face tones, so small slope differences are hard to read; and the dark hexagonal silhouette behind shares no edge or calibration with the light surface.
6. The single most confusing aspect is the large, very dark hexagonal silhouette behind the light surface. It is much larger than the surface, does not share its orientation or edges, and carries no visible shading cues that explain what it is (floor plane, shadow, or backdrop), and it provides no scale. A secondary confusion is whether the frame 1 convergence point touches the far edge or sits just inside it, which is near the limit of what the faint lines allow me to resolve.
